notes: Check batch 2026-10-30-check-3 for order-report: four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so opus is unavailable in per_rule. All four have rc 0 and model_id matching their tier; each result.json records head 551e3ab with uncommitted true and skill_hash 7bfdb63a..., which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the current idiomatic-elixir/ folder, and every transcript contains the renamed clause rule ("unless the clauses are a table", "A table may end in one fallback row") and the with rule's tail-call sentence ("is a tail call, not a second step"). skills_listed is 83 for haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 and 70 for haiku-2. All four read SKILL.md only, so Expected reads (none) is met in all four. In the scratch folder all four pass mix format --check-formatted, compile with no warning against a stand-in Decimal written there (the run folders have no Decimal dependency, which is why compiles carries Decimal warnings), and pass their doctests (haiku-1 1, sonnet-1 2, sonnet-2 1; haiku-2 has none). A probe gave correct per-currency totals (19.99 + 0.01 EUR = 20.00), last-order dates (a -02:00 order at 23:30 falls on the next UTC day in all four), a refunded-only customer left out of top_customers, empty results for [] and {:error, ...} for a missing key, a bad amount, an unknown status and a bad date. Sonnet-1 reports a missing key as :invalid_order without naming the key; no rule in the list covers this, so it is noted in its summary only.

The clause rule is graded against its current text under its new heading, "Put each `->` clause body on its own line unless the clauses are a table"; earlier grade files graded "Break a `->` clause whose pattern and body together pass 70 characters", so there is no earlier verdict to match. Deciding sentences: "A clause of `case`, `cond`, `with ... else` or `receive` puts its body on the line after the `->`" for every broken case, and "When one clause carries the result forward and another converts, reports or reraises, the clauses do different jobs and are not a table, however short each line is" plus "A table may end in one fallback row that reports what did not match" for the one one-line case. No run writes cond, receive or with ... else. Every case, by run. Haiku-1: line 90 case parse_order(row) inside reduce_while ({:ok, order} -> / {:error, _reason} = error ->), broken; lines 122-126 case Map.fetch(row, key) with three one-line clauses, line 123 {:ok, value} when is_binary(value) -> {:ok, value}, line 124 {:ok, _value} -> {:error, {:invalid_field, key}}, line 125 :error -> {:error, {:missing_field, key}}: not a table, because line 123 passes the value through while lines 124-125 report errors, and two error rows exceed the one fallback row, so violated; line 130 case Decimal.parse(text) ({amount, ""} -> / {_amount, _rest} -> / :error ->), broken; line 143 case DateTime.from_iso8601(text) ({:ok, placed_at, _offset} -> / {:error, _reason} ->), broken. Haiku-2: line 43 case parse_order(row) in reduce_while (two clauses), broken; lines 75-84 case Map.fetch(row, key), the same three clauses as haiku-1's one-line case, broken with blank lines; line 88 case Decimal.parse(text) (three clauses), broken; line 102 case DateTime.from_iso8601(text) (two clauses), broken. Sonnet-1: line 120 case Decimal.parse(text) (three clauses), broken; line 135 case DateTime.from_iso8601(text) (two clauses), broken. Sonnet-2: line 98 case parse_order(row) ({:ok, order} -> tail call / {:error, reason} -> {:error, {:invalid_order, index, reason}}), broken; line 145 case Decimal.parse(text) (three clauses), broken; line 166 case DateTime.from_iso8601(text) (two clauses), broken. No run writes a case that is a table; the parse_status/1 status mapping, the rule's own table example, is written as function clauses in all four. The rule's last sentence on a fn argument defers to the captures rule, so haiku-1's one-line fn at line 84 is graded there, not here, as 2026-10-30-check-2 held. Result: haiku 1 of 2 violated (haiku-1), sonnet 0 of 2.

The with rule is graded against its current text. Deciding sentences: "One step is a `with` only when its body cannot fail and there is no `else`, so the `with` does nothing but pass the error through; any other one-step `with` is a `case`", "A `case` whose error clause is `{:error, _reason} = error -> error` is the same pass-through spelled out over four lines; write it as the `with`", and "A body that is one call whose `{:ok, value}` or `{:error, reason}` goes out as the function's own result, the recursive `parse_rows(rest, [order | orders])` of a hand-written loop, is a tail call, not a second step, and the one-step `with` stays". All four write build/1 as a one-step with whose body builds the report and cannot fail, no else (haiku-1 lines 35-37, haiku-2 lines 36-38, sonnet-1 lines 79-81, sonnet-2 lines 84-86). Sonnet-1's parse_orders/2 (lines 88-92) is a one-step with whose body is the tail call parse_orders(rest, [order | orders]), clean under the tail-call sentence; 2026-10-30-check-2 graded the same shape in its haiku-1 as violated under the text before that sentence existed. Sonnet-2's parse_orders/2 (lines 97-105) is a case whose error clause adds the row index, {:error, reason} -> {:error, {:invalid_order, index, reason}}, so it maps the error and stays a case. No run writes a pass-through case: the reduce_while cases (haiku-1 line 90, haiku-2 line 43) turn the result into {:cont, ...} or {:halt, error}. The multi-step withs have eight steps (haiku-1, haiku-2), three (sonnet-1) or five (sonnet-2), none with an else or a nested case. 0 of 4 violated.

The captures rule is graded against its current text. Deciding sentences: "A `fn` that binds names takes the room its names earn: the body goes on the line after the `->`, and `end` closes it on a line of its own" with "A one-line `fn {name, kind} -> {name, root_view(doc, name, kind)} end` is a capture that could not be written, squeezed onto the head's line", and "When the body does more than one call, would need `&3`, or passes `&2` before `&1` or the same placeholder twice, write `fn` with named arguments". Every fn binds names. Haiku-1: lines 52-54, 68-70 and 89-97 are multi-line; line 84 |> Enum.sort_by(fn {customer_id, count} -> {-count, customer_id} end) is one line, violated. Haiku-2: lines 42-50 and 140-142 multi-line; line 154 |> Enum.sort_by(&{-&1.completed_count, &1.customer_id}) uses &1 twice, violated (the same capture its tier wrote in 2026-10-30-check-2). Sonnet-1: lines 155-157, 172-174, 181-183 multi-line, clean. Sonnet-2: lines 186-188, 207-209, 216-218 multi-line; line 208 &Decimal.add(&1.amount, &2) is the rule's own example; line 133 &(not Map.has_key?(row, &1)) is one operator over one call, the shape of the Enum table's own &(File.read!(&1) =~ ~r/Yex/), held clean. Result: haiku 2 of 2 violated, sonnet 0 of 2.

Other rules in the list, same standard as 2026-10-23/grades/order-report-skill.json and the 2026-10-30 check batches. The do: rule (reworded since d04061d): every do: body is a tuple or a single call (parse_status/1 clauses everywhere; sonnet-1 lines 84, 86, 117, 132, 144; sonnet-2 lines 95, 136, 142, 157, 163, 175); sonnet-1 line 187 defp completed(orders), do: Enum.filter(orders, &(&1.status == :completed)) holds a capture of a comparison, not "a capture that carries a call with arguments of its own", held clean as the 2026-10-23 sweep held opus-1's identical line; sonnet-2's parse_customer_id/1 and parse_currency/1 (lines 138-140, 159-161) write a one-expression body under a long guard as a block, which the rule allows; every block clause beside a do: clause is set apart by a blank line; no run writes if or for. Pipelines: no pipeline on one line, none pipes a single step, none starts with a kind or mode argument. Enum/Map: all four group with Enum.group_by then Map.new (haiku-2 then Enum.map into structs); haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 count with frequencies_by, haiku-2 counts the filtered list that also feeds the totals (Enum.count, line 132), held clean as before; the Decimal sums with Enum.reduce are reductions no table row replaces. Lists: haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 prepend without reversing, held clean as before because nothing downstream depends on the order; sonnet-1 reverses. Naming, dates, money, atoms and processes: all four clean. Outside the list: haiku-2's build/1 @doc has no ## Examples and its Order struct has no @type t, as earlier batches listed the same shapes; sonnet-1's {:ok, %Order{...}} at lines 106-113 is a returned tuple, not a call argument; the multi-line heads of sonnet-1's and sonnet-2's parse_order/1 bind the five required keys with a catch-all clause below, so the keys select by presence. No other violation was found.
